Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Object 2 Flow of Play 3 Roll 4 Score 5 Buy Object Get the most points by rolling dice to mark off fruit skewers. The game ends when someone fills 50 hearts by marking skewers. Play until everyone has had the same number of turns, and then highest score wins. Flow of Play Each turn, go through these 3 phases: Roll Roll all 5 white dice to try and make the best possible fruit skewer (aka. dice combination) If your roll would allow more than one skewer, you get to choose which one to score. Possibilities are: Pair - 2 identical fruits Three of a kind - 3 identical fruits Full house - 3 identical fruits and 2 other identical fruits Four of a kind - 4 identical fruits Straight - 5 different fruits Yums - 5 identical fruits You may reroll, ONCE, as many dice as you wish. Score Circle the next free box for the skewer you made. Score Hearts (in other words points) and Bonus tokens depending on the skewer you made. Be aware that the bonuses are different on each score sheet. If the heart track is full, take the remainder in stars; the end of the game triggers. If no skewer scores, mark off a "catch-up" space - you'll get the associated bonus. For every cross rolled, the other players cross off a free scoring box of their choice. They get the bonuses but not the points. If you mark (either circle or cross out) all the scoring boxes in the first column, score 3 stars. Bonuses are: Reroll token - Spend a reroll token to reroll dice an extra time Stars - Stars are spent in the buy round, or are each a point at the end of the game Red Die - Spend before rolling to add the red die. The red die has a wild marshmallow face instead of a cross. Buy Buy a Yums card to obtain powerful effects Choose a card from the display, paying stars based on it's position. Cards slide down to fill. [Rating: 3/10] Un croisement entre le Yam's et Candy Crush. Autrement dit, une pluie de points pour récompenser votre cerveau avec de la dopamine à chaque coup, ici un lancer de dés. Je préfère la tension que procure le Yam's.

[Rating: 3/10] A roll and write game where players rolls dice rolls (maybe rerolls), fills in a set (like yahtzee), and gaining a card/power that may be used for future turns. Player with the most points wins. This game reminds me of yahtzee.

[Rating: 5/10] BGA, the cards make it more asymmetrical which I thawt would be interesting but actually just makes the randomness more random lmao

[Rating: 5/10] Nothing much new in this genre aside from cards?  Digital   youtube.com/amassgames

[Rating: 5/10] Initial Thoughts: A broken combo early in the game can really run away. Not necessarily a bad thing, given how light and quick the game is.    Played on BGA

[Rating: 5/10] Utterly forgettable fruit-themed roll-and-write game that I only played online (on Boardgamearena). 2-5 players. Rating based on one play.

[Rating: 5/10] Cute and nicely produced. However, at higher player counts,  the game drags on forever overstaying its welcome so much that the only thing you remember is how relieved you felt when it was finally over.  It's quite possible with only 2-3 people at the table it works better. I guess I'll never know.

[Rating: 5/10] Un roll'n write amusant, mais au look acidulé un peu trop chargé. Ça fonctionne, mais il manque un petit quelque chose pour le rendre vraiment accrocheur. Il a l'air de plaire à pas mal de monde, mais il manque à mon avis un peu de cleaning pour le rendre plus fluide et plus fun. Bref, un peu amusant mais sans réel goût de reviens-y.
